about: Records whose values in the two-build comparison differ from the baseline build on purpose: the baseline is wrong there. compare_builds.py accepts a difference only for a listed (database, variant, kind, record) and prints how many it accepted. Remove the entries when the baseline tag moves past the fix.

rounding_limit.reason: Differences between 1e-12 and 1e-10 on the whole grid: 39 on 2026-10-30, on the local build and in CI. Parameters and V pass through SI (decision 0022). A change that raises the count above this limit updates it in the same commit, and says why.

changes.reason: The baseline returned cached values that depend on the calculation order: the reactants of a reaction-defined substance are calculated with the gas pressure correction on, and shared the cache with the plain calculations. The new values equal the values without memoization (all 2928 checked). Test: pytests/test_calculation_order.py.

Now each is converted to the canonical convention after its method; asking for the native convention gives the baseline values (tests/extra_models).

Conventions (R4.5): AkinfievDiamond03 reads G, H and S of water. The baseline gave it water in the output convention, so asking for the steam tables changed these solutes by the reference of water. Inside the engine water is now canonical: these solutes equal the default variant.

Conventions (R4.5): the baseline calculated a substance from its defining reaction with the reactants in the output convention. Their reactions have H2O@, so the reference of water reached them. Now it is calculated in the canonical convention and converted once.

Conventions (R4.5): the baseline calculated a substance from its defining reaction with the reactants in the output convention. Water is not converted to Berman-Brown, so G was wrong by the coefficient of H2O@ times Tr times the element entropies of water (69.5 kJ/mol for each H2O@). Now it is calculated in the canonical convention and converted once.
